treatmentJourney.title: Initial Consultation & Planning
treatmentJourney.description: Your journey begins with a thorough examination, including 3D imaging if needed, to assess your oral health, discuss your goals, and develop a personalized treatment plan for your dental implants.

treatmentJourney.title: Preparation & Foundation Work
treatmentJourney.description: Any necessary preparatory procedures, such as extractions of failing teeth or bone grafting to ensure adequate bone density, will be performed to create an ideal foundation for your implants.

treatmentJourney.title: Implant Placement Surgery
treatmentJourney.description: The precise surgical placement of the titanium implant post into your jawbone. This procedure is performed with care, and sedation options like Nitrous Oxide are available for your comfort.

treatmentJourney.title: Healing & Osseointegration
treatmentJourney.description: A crucial healing period follows, during which the implant fuses with your jawbone in a process called osseointegration. This typically takes several months and is vital for long-term stability.

treatmentJourney.title: Abutment Placement & Impressions
treatmentJourney.description: Once osseointegration is complete, a small connector piece called an abutment is placed on the implant. We then take precise impressions to custom-craft your new crown, bridge, or arch.

treatmentJourney.title: Final Restoration & Care Plan
treatmentJourney.description: Your custom-made crown, bridge, or full arch is securely attached to the implant. We provide detailed instructions for care to ensure the longevity of your new, confident smile.

faqItems.question: How long does the entire implant process take?
faqItems.answer: The dental implant process typically spans several months. It involves initial consultation, any necessary preparatory work like bone grafting, implant placement, a healing period for osseointegration, and finally, the placement of your custom crown or restoration.

faqItems.question: Am I a candidate for dental implants if I have bone loss?
faqItems.answer: Even with some bone loss, many patients can still be candidates for dental implants. We offer bone grafting procedures to build up the jawbone, creating a stable foundation for the implant, ensuring successful placement and long-term stability.

faqItems.question: How long do dental implants last?
faqItems.answer: With proper oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups, dental implants are designed to be a long-term solution and can last for many decades, often for a lifetime. The crown or bridge may need replacement after 10-15 years, but the implant post itself is very durable.

faqItems.question: Is implant surgery painful, and what sedation do you offer?
faqItems.answer: We prioritize your comfort during implant surgery. We use local anesthesia to numb the area, and for patients with dental anxiety, we offer Nitrous Oxide Sedation to ensure a relaxed and pain-free experience during your procedure.

faqItems.question: What is the best option: implants, bridges, or dentures?
faqItems.answer: The best option depends on your individual needs and oral health. Dental implants offer the most natural look and feel, preserving bone and requiring no support from adjacent teeth. We will discuss all suitable options during your consultation to determine the ideal solution for you.

faqItems.question: Are you accepting new patients for dental implant consultations?
faqItems.answer: Yes, we are always excited to welcome new patients to United Smiles Family Dental. We encourage you to schedule an initial consultation to discuss your specific needs and explore how dental implants can restore your smile and oral health.
